summary: Summary PRT_SHAPE bug was logging-only. Runtime uses per-layer g_prt_sidecar_M[]/N[] correctly. Fix to cli.cpp now reports accurate summary M/N from first-loaded sidecar.

bug_investigation.summary_shape_source: tools/cli/cli.cpp line ~478: hardcoded 896/4864 literals in fprintf
bug_investigation.per_layer_shape_source: llama_set_prt_sidecar() in src/llama.cpp: sets g_prt_sidecar_M[layer]=M, g_prt_sidecar_N[layer]=N
bug_investigation.runtime_shape_source: prt_graph_replace.h: uses g_prt_sidecar_M[i]/g_prt_sidecar_N[i] directly (correct per-layer values)
bug_investigation.reason: The hardcoded 896/4864 in the summary log printf only affected the log output. The actual PRT kernel and all per-layer logging used the correct per-layer arrays.

fix.change: Replaced hardcoded 896/4864 literals in PRT_SHAPE summary log with values read from g_prt_sidecar_M[0] and g_prt_sidecar_N[0]

root_cause_explained.symptom: Summary PRT_SHAPE log showed M=896 N=4864 (stale 0.5B values) while per-layer sidecar logs showed M=2048 N=11008
root_cause_explained.root_cause: cli.cpp used hardcoded literal values 896 and 4864 instead of reading from the global arrays
root_cause_explained.impact: Logging-only. The runtime custom op used g_prt_sidecar_M[i]/N[i] per-layer correctly throughout all prior runs
root_cause_explained.why_no_prior_impact: The summary log was cosmetic — it just printed expected values for the human reading the log. Actual PRT kernel used per-layer M/N correctly.
